items.stem: At an end-of-tranche review, projected benefits have fallen below the threshold that justified the programme. The most appropriate governance action is to:

options.text: Reassess the business case and decide whether to continue, change or stop
options.rationale: Correct: end-of-tranche reviews exist to make continue/change/stop decisions on evidence.

options.text: Automatically start the next tranche regardless
options.rationale: Proceeding blindly ignores the review's purpose.

options.text: Hide the shortfall from the sponsoring group

items.explanation: Correct: end-of-tranche reviews exist to make continue/change/stop decisions on evidence.
items.domain_ref: Tranches, risk and transition in context

items.stem: When the organisation's strategy changes significantly, the programme blueprint should be:

options.text: Reviewed and revised to reflect the new target state
options.rationale: Correct: the blueprint must track strategic change.
A frozen blueprint can drive the programme to the wrong target.
The blueprint is needed; it is revised, not deleted.
Ignoring it risks delivering the wrong outcome.

items.explanation: Correct: the blueprint must track strategic change.

items.stem: Which TWO are valid reasons to re-baseline a benefits profile mid-programme? (Select TWO)

options.text: A key assumption behind the benefit has changed
A strategic change altered the target outcome
options.rationale: Correct: strategic change can change expected benefits.

options.text: The programme manager prefers rounder numbers
options.rationale: Personal preference is not a valid reason.

options.text: To make the dashboard look greener
Because a tranche review is inconvenient
options.rationale: Avoiding scrutiny is not a valid reason.

items.explanation: Correct: changed assumptions justify re-baselining. Correct: strategic change can change expected benefits.
